thread:
meera: Heads up — the canary deploy for AWQ group-size sweep (g=32,64,128) on rtx-pool-2 started hitting sporadic decode stalls at ~10k qps. Observed after ~3h.
alex: Logs?
meera: Pasting tail of runner logs:
```
[2026-03-15 13:12:34] runner: decode loop stalled, kv_cache mismatch, seq=512, group=64
[2026-03-15 13:12:34] runtime: retried slice failed: -EAGAIN
[2026-03-15 13:12:35] trace: p99 latency 1.8s -> 3.2s
```
jia: Is this only with act-quant enabled?
meera: Good question — we were testing two axes: act_quant={0,4} and group_size={32,64,128}. The failures only appear when act_quant=4 and group_size>=64.
sam: Could be numeric noise with large group aggregation. Any eval drift?
meera: Yes, eval run on devset shows 0.7% top1 drop for group64+act4 vs fp16 baseline, but the bigger concern is serving instability.
ciara: Have we ruled out a batching edge? What does batcher telemetry show?
meera: Batcher logs show group coalescing hitting 512-token windows, KV prefetches racing. snippet:
```
batcher: merged 5 reqs -> group=64 total_tokens=4096
prefetch: kv_alloc 0.9ms, apply_actq 2.3ms
```
alex: That prefactor of apply_actq looks suspect. Can you dump kernel timings from the Q slot?
meera: Attached kernel profiler output (summary): apply_actq kernel time spikes to 40ms for group>=64 occasionally.
quant-bot: Rollout status: canary 23% -> paused (manual) due to instability alerts :warning:
jia: Two hypotheses: (1) act-quant accumulation overflow in accumulation buffer; (2) misaligned vector loads when group>32 on newer cudnn/torch kernels.
sam: Quick repro on local devbox with smaller batch? Anyone can repro in staging?
meera: I repro'd in staging VM with 2 concurrent clients hitting seq512, group64, act4. Steps:
```
python load_test.py --model redwood-7b-awq --group 64 --act_quant 4 --concurrency 2 --seq 512
```
meera: Outcome: intermittent `decoder hang` requiring kill -9; stack shows stuck in apply_act_quant_cuda.
ciara: Let's bisect: try group=48? does instability threshold at power-of-two?
alex: Also check quantization order flags — there's a recent commit that toggles `actq_use_shared_scratch=True` in docker image `infer:v2026-03-01`.
meera: Rebuilt with `actq_use_shared_scratch=False` — running overnight.
jia: If this is a race in scratch memory, toggling shared scratch should help. Also try running with `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.7` to stress allocation.
sam: Any workaround we can use for canary? Rollback to act_quant=0 on production for affected model and keep group tune at 32 maybe.
meera: I've paused canary and applied temporary policy: act_quant=0 for redwood-7b-awq in prod. Can confirm old baseline stable.
quant-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-042 awq-actq-stability. Assigned to eng-ml.
alex: Next steps: 1) repro and attach nvprof traces; 2) run unit with memory sanitizer if possible; 3) test `actq_use_shared_scratch=False` across permutations. I'll take nvprof.
meera: Thanks. Also cross-check eval quality delta on subset: group64+act4 shows longer tail token-level perplexity increase in dialogue prompts.
ciara: I'll schedule a small A/B test with conservative routing (75% baseline, 25% canary) after rollback to validate patch.
meera: Posting logs to #eng-sre and linking PR with diff of actq scratch flag: https://git.internal/repo/awq/PR-412
alex: Good. Let's sync tomorrow 11:00 instandup. :thumbsup:
